name: PÚKK
description: Púkk (often spelled 'Pukk') is a traditional Icelandic card game that belongs to the ancient 'Poch' family. It involves a unique betting layout (traditionally a series of dishes or a special mat) and three distinct phases of play: Dressing the Board, Vying (the 'Púkk' phase), and Shedding (the 'Play' phase). It is famous for its 'Pamfíll' (Jack of Clubs) which acts as a powerful wild card. Púkk is a game of social interaction, bluffing, and sequence-building that has been an Icelandic family staple for centuries.

Púkk is a game of social interaction, bluffing, and sequence-building that has been an Icelandic family staple for centuries.
Derived from the 15th-century German game 'Pochen' and the French 'Poque'. It arrived in Iceland and evolved into its current form with localized terminology and the specific 'Pamfíll' mechanic.
40-card pack, Púkk betting layout (mat or set of dishes/pools), chips.

items.text: Minimum pair of sixes: Some require that a player hold a combination no lower than a pair of 6s to púkk (enter the vying phase).
Pamfíll cannot substitute for Six: Some players do not permit Pamfíll to substitute for a Six in the vying hand ranking.
